hints.title: Bound Consecutive Laps on One Tire
hints.text: Because r >= 2, the time for lap x grows exponentially. Running more than 17 consecutive laps on any single tire is never optimal compared to changing tires.

hints.title: Precompute Best Tire Times
hints.text: Calculate min_tire[x], the minimum time to complete x consecutive laps without changing tires across all available tires.

hints.title: 1D Dynamic Programming Over Laps
hints.text: Let dp[i] be the minimum time to finish i laps. Try all possible lengths j (1 to 17) for the final tire run.

hints.title: Complete Python Solution

complexity.notes: Exponential tire degradation with bounded consecutive laps.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing permutations of tire swaps over 1000 laps is doubly exponential.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Bounding single-tire runs to 17 laps limits the inner DP loop to a small constant.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Prove the ~17 lap upper bound before setting up 1D dynamic programming.

solutions.approach: Python bounded consecutive lap precomputation and 1D DP.
JavaScript array precomputation and loop DP.
